guide.summary: Shopify OAuth runs through an app you create in the Dev Dashboard under a Partner organization. Your first decision is permanent: public distribution or custom distribution. An agent whose users are many unrelated merchants needs public distribution, which means App Store registration, a one-time fee and Shopify review. Custom distribution needs no approval, but it can only reach a single store or stores in one Plus organization. Tokens are issued per shop, and Shopify wants public apps on expiring offline tokens with refresh tokens. Review duration and the fee amount are not documented here.
auth_alternatives: Client credentials grant: choose it if the agent only acts on stores in your own organization. It skips merchant authorization entirely, but it cannot serve other merchants' stores.

Custom distribution with an install link: choose it for a single merchant or one Plus organization. No Shopify approval is needed, but the distribution choice is permanent and the app cannot reach unrelated stores.

Token exchange (embedded apps): choose it if the app runs embedded in the Shopify admin. It swaps an ID token for an access token without redirecting the merchant, but it does not fit a standalone agent.

reasons_to_bring_own: Composio does not offer managed auth for Shopify, so you need your own app credentials.
Reaching many merchants requires your own publicly distributed app, which must pass Shopify review.
build_or_borrow.verdict: Build your own Shopify app, because Composio has no managed auth for Shopify; pick public distribution if your agent serves unrelated merchants, or use the client credentials grant if it only touches your own organization's stores.

prerequisites.text: The app must belong to a Partner organization. Otherwise the Distribution card does not appear in the Dev Dashboard.
Get the client ID and client secret from the Dev Dashboard.
Register your redirect URI in the Dev Dashboard app settings or in the [auth] section of shopify.app.toml.
For public distribution, register for the Shopify App Store. This has a one-time fee; the amount is not stated in these sources.
Before review, meet the App Store review page requirements.

oauth.token_lifetime: Expiring offline access tokens last 1 hour, and their refresh tokens last 90 days when issued. Online tokens expire after 24 hours or when the user logs out of the Shopify admin.
redirect_uri_rules: The redirect URI must be added in the Dev Dashboard app settings or in the [auth] section of shopify.app.toml.

blockers.text: The distribution method (public or custom) cannot be changed after you select it.
blockers.workaround: Decide before clicking. For a multi-merchant agent, choose public distribution. If you also need custom installs, create a separate app for them.

blockers.text: Public distribution requires Shopify approval. The review duration is not documented here.
blockers.workaround: Meet the App Store review requirements before you submit. Use a custom-distribution or client-credentials app on your own stores for development in the meantime.

blockers.text: Apps that fail core requirements are moved to Paused status.
blockers.workaround: Keep meeting the review requirements after you publish.

blockers.text: Public apps still using non-expiring offline tokens will be delisted and blocked from new installs on January 1, 2027.
blockers.workaround: Implement expiring offline tokens with refresh from the start.

blockers.text: Some scopes grant access to protected customer data, and those scopes add requirements.
blockers.workaround: Request only the scopes you need, and justify any protected customer data scopes.

app_specific_gotchas.text: The token endpoint is per shop (https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token). Store the shop domain alongside each token.
Shopify serves no OAuth or OpenID discovery document, so configure endpoints by hand.
Expiring offline tokens last only 1 hour, and their refresh tokens last 90 days. Refresh proactively, or merchants will have to reconnect.
Unpublished public apps that skip approval were deprecated in December 2019. Multi-merchant reach means review.
Custom apps reach multiple stores only within the same Plus organization.

steps.title: Set up a Partner organization and create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail_md:
Log in and make sure the app belongs to a **Partner organization**. The Distribution card, which you need in step 3, only appears for apps in a Partner organization. Create the app in the Dev Dashboard. This is also where the client ID and client secret come from.

Composio lists no managed auth for Shopify, so plan on using your own app credentials.

steps.title: Lay out the distribution trade-off before anything is locked in
steps.detail_md:
The agent writes up the choice for the developer.

- **Public distribution**
  - Requires Shopify approval.
  - Requires App Store registration, which has a one-time fee. The amount is not covered here.
  - Can be installed on multiple stores.
- **Custom distribution**
  - Needs no approval.
  - Is installed through an install link sent to the store owner.
  - Can only reach multiple stores inside the same Plus organization.
- **Constraints on the choice**
  - Apps that use App Home UI extensions can only use custom distribution.
  - The old unpublished-app route, a public app with no approval, was deprecated in December 2019. There is no middle path.

**Opinion:** if your agent's users are unrelated merchants, custom distribution will not scale, and public distribution is the realistic choice.

steps.title: Choose the distribution method (irreversible)
steps.detail_md:
In the Dev Dashboard, open the app's Home and select public or custom on the **Distribution** card.

This cannot be changed after selection. A wrong choice means starting over with a new app, so make this decision deliberately.

steps.title: Draft the redirect URI list and the scope list
steps.detail_md:
The agent lists the following:

- **Redirect URIs:** every callback URL the integration will use, covering local, staging and production.
- **Scopes:** the minimal access scopes as a comma-separated list. The specific scope names your agent needs are not covered by the provided material, so derive them from the features you build.

Flag any scope that grants **protected customer data** access, because those scopes add requirements.

steps.title: Register redirect URIs and store credentials
steps.detail_md: Add the redirect URIs in the Dev Dashboard app settings, or in the `[auth]` section of `shopify.app.toml`. Then copy the client ID and client secret from the Dev Dashboard into your secrets store.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth authorization code flow
steps.detail_md:
Standalone and API-only apps use the **authorization code grant**. The merchant approves or denies the permissions prompt that Shopify shows. Your server then exchanges the code at `POST https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token`.

There is no discovery document on shopify.com: both `.well-known` probes returned 404. Hardcode the endpoints rather than relying on discovery.

The authorize URL is not covered by the provided claims. Take it from shopify.dev rather than guessing.

Other grants, and when they apply:
- **Embedded apps** use token exchange instead.
- **Apps acting only on your own organization's stores** can use the client credentials grant, which skips merchant authorization. That does not fit an agent serving outside merchants.

steps.title: Use expiring offline tokens with refresh
steps.detail_md:
Use expiring offline access tokens, which last 1 hour. Store the refresh token, which lasts 90 days when issued, and refresh before expiry.

This is not optional for a public app. Public apps still on non-expiring offline tokens will be delisted and blocked from new installs on **January 1, 2027**.

Online tokens expire after 24 hours or when the user logs out of the admin. That makes them a poor fit for a background agent.

steps.title: Test the full install and token flow on a store you control
steps.detail_md:
Log in, install the app, approve the permissions prompt, confirm the code exchange works, and confirm a refresh works.

How to obtain a test store is not covered by the provided claims.

steps.title: Custom path only: generate and send install links
steps.detail_md:
If you chose custom distribution, generate the install link in the Dev Dashboard and send it to the store owner, who installs the app. No App Store listing or review is involved.

The multi-store option is optional. Clear it to limit the app to one store.

Multi-store installs only work within one Plus organization.

Skip steps 10 to 13 on this path.

steps.title: Public path: register for the Shopify App Store and pay the fee
steps.detail_md: Public distribution requires App Store registration with a one-time fee. The fee amount is not covered by the provided claims.

steps.title: Draft listing and review materials
steps.detail_md:
The agent prepares the listing content against the **App Store review page requirements**. Public apps must meet these before they are reviewed. The requirements are the same for fully visible and limited visibility apps, so limited visibility is not a shortcut.

Include justification for any protected customer data scopes.

The exact requirement list is not reproduced in the provided claims.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail_md: Submit the app. It moves from **Draft** to **Submitted**.

steps.title: Shopify review
steps.detail_md:
Shopify owns this step. The status moves through Submitted, Reviewed and Published. Apps failing core requirements are moved to **Paused**.

Review duration is **not documented** in the provided claims. The 0 minutes shown for this step is a placeholder, not an estimate.

steps.title: Fix any findings, then share the install with users
steps.detail_md: If the app is Paused, fix the failed core requirements and resubmit. Once the app is Published, any merchant can connect it through the OAuth flow from step 6.

belief_diff.topic: Does letting arbitrary users connect require provider review or verification?
belief_diff.prior_belief: Yes, a public Shopify app must pass Shopify's app review before merchants outside the development store can install it, while custom or unlisted apps can be installed directly by a specific merchant without review.
belief_diff.finding: Claims confirm public distribution requires Shopify approval and custom distribution does not, and custom apps are installed via a generated install link sent to the store owner.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Shopify app review typically takes about 5 to 10 business days, though resubmissions after failed checks can add another week.
belief_diff.finding: The claims list review statuses (Draft, Submitted, Reviewed, Published) but give no review duration or resubmission timing.

belief_diff.topic: Limits while the app is unapproved
belief_diff.prior_belief: Unlisted apps in development can be installed on up to 10 development stores, and an unreviewed public app cannot be installed by merchants outside the partner's own development stores.
belief_diff.finding: Claims say unpublished apps were deprecated in December 2019 and that custom apps can be installed on multiple stores only within the same Plus organization, but they do not state the 10-development-store limit or the install restriction for unreviewed public apps.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Creating a Partner account and building apps is free, but apps that charge merchants must use Shopify Billing, which takes a 20% revenue share on app charges (reduced to 15% for qualifying developers earning under $1 million per year).
belief_diff.finding: Claims only say public distribution requires registering for the App Store with a one-time fee; they do not address Partner account cost, Shopify Billing, or revenue share percentages.

belief_diff.topic: Key prerequisites (domain, privacy policy, video, business verification)
belief_diff.prior_belief: A public app requires an HTTPS app URL on a domain you control, a privacy policy URL, a demo or setup video, and a Partner account with accurate business details, but no separate formal business verification step.
belief_diff.finding: Claims say public apps must meet App Store review page requirements and that a Partner organization is needed for the Distribution card, but do not list the specific URL, privacy policy, video, or business verification requirements.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Redirect URLs must be HTTPS and exactly match an entry in the app's allowed redirection URL list in the Partner dashboard, with localhost permitted only for development.
belief_diff.finding: Claims say the redirect URI must be added in the Dev Dashboard app settings or the [auth] section of shopify.app.toml, but say nothing about the HTTPS requirement, exact matching, or localhost exception.
